name: West African farming peoples
summary: The many farming peoples of the West African savannah and forest edge, who domesticated pearl millet, African rice and yams. The Nok culture made some of Africa’s oldest sculptures and smelted iron. On the map, this covers areas not shown as particular kingdoms.

knownFor.label: Nok terracottas
knownFor.note: Clay heads and figures made in central Nigeria about 2,500 years ago.

knownFor.label: African rice
knownFor.note: Rice domesticated separately in the inland Niger delta.

knownFor.label: Pearl millet
knownFor.note: A drought-tough grain first grown in the West African Sahel.

location.value: The savannah and forest edge of West Africa, from Senegal to Lake Chad. (The source border maps stretch this zone across the whole Sahel belt to the Horn of Africa.)
location.source: Wikipedia: Nok culture; Wikipedia: History of West Africa

terrain.value: Grassland, river valleys (Niger, Benue, Senegal) and the edge of the rainforest.
terrain.source: Wikipedia: Nok culture; Wikipedia: History of West Africa

climate.value: Tropical, with one rainy season in the north and two near the coast; the Sahara grew drier after about 3000 BCE.
climate.source: Wikipedia: Nok culture; Wikipedia: History of West Africa

resources.value: Farmland for millet, sorghum, rice and yams; iron ore; shea and oil palms.
resources.source: Wikipedia: Nok culture; Wikipedia: History of West Africa

disasters.source: Wikipedia: Nok culture; Wikipedia: History of West Africa

population.value: Unknown; populations grew as farming spread.
population.source: Wikipedia: Nok culture; Wikipedia: History of West Africa

urbanisation.value: Mostly villages; early towns such as Jenne-Jeno (from about 250 BCE).
urbanisation.source: Wikipedia: Nok culture; Wikipedia: History of West Africa

disease.source: Wikipedia: Nok culture; Wikipedia: History of West Africa

migration.value: Farmers moved south as the Sahara dried; Mande- and Niger-Congo-speaking peoples spread widely.
migration.source: Wikipedia: Nok culture; Wikipedia: History of West Africa

economicBase.value: Pearl millet was domesticated near Dhar Tichitt by about 1900–1700 BCE (fully by at least 1100 BCE); pearl millet and cowpeas are the only crops known from the Nok.
economicBase.source: Wikipedia: Dhar Tichitt and Nok culture (checked 13 Nov 2026)

tradeRoutes.value: Exchange along the Niger River; later the trans-Saharan trade.
tradeRoutes.source: Wikipedia: Nok culture; Wikipedia: History of West Africa

wealth.source: Wikipedia: Nok culture; Wikipedia: History of West Africa

moneyAndTax.value: No money in early times; later cowrie shells and iron bars.
moneyAndTax.source: Wikipedia: Nok culture; Wikipedia: History of West Africa

inequality.value: Varied, from equal villages to societies with chiefs and craft castes.
inequality.source: Wikipedia: Nok culture; Wikipedia: History of West Africa

governmentType.value: Villages led by elders and lineage heads; many later formed chiefdoms and kingdoms.
governmentType.source: Wikipedia: Nok culture; Wikipedia: History of West Africa

keyRulers.value: No early rulers are known by name.
keyRulers.source: Wikipedia: Nok culture; Wikipedia: History of West Africa

succession.source: Wikipedia: Nok culture; Wikipedia: History of West Africa

institutions.value: Councils of elders, age groups and secret societies.
institutions.source: Wikipedia: Nok culture; Wikipedia: History of West Africa

stability.source: Wikipedia: Nok culture; Wikipedia: History of West Africa

eliteConflict.source: Wikipedia: Nok culture; Wikipedia: History of West Africa

armyAndTech.source: Wikipedia: Nok culture; Wikipedia: History of West Africa

majorWars.source: Wikipedia: Nok culture; Wikipedia: History of West Africa

territoryChange.value: Farming spread steadily across the region.
territoryChange.source: Wikipedia: Nok culture; Wikipedia: History of West Africa

alliancesRivals.value: Traded with Saharan herders and later with the empires of Ghana and Mali.
alliancesRivals.source: Wikipedia: Nok culture; Wikipedia: History of West Africa

inventions.value: Nok iron metallurgy may have developed between 750 and 550 BCE and the earliest Nok terracotta sculptures around 900 BCE; their purpose is unknown.

scienceEducation.value: Knowledge passed on orally; griots (praise singers) kept histories.
scienceEducation.source: Wikipedia: Nok culture; Wikipedia: History of West Africa

openness.value: Open to new crops and ideas through trade.
openness.source: Wikipedia: Nok culture; Wikipedia: History of West Africa

communicationTransport.value: Footpaths and canoes on the Niger and Benue rivers; donkeys in the north.
communicationTransport.source: Wikipedia: Nok culture; Wikipedia: History of West Africa

religion.value: Traditional religions with ancestors and nature spirits; Islam spread later.
religion.source: Wikipedia: Nok culture; Wikipedia: History of West Africa

languageWriting.value: Many Niger-Congo and Mande languages; no writing in early times.
languageWriting.source: Wikipedia: Nok culture; Wikipedia: History of West Africa

artsArchitecture.value: Nok terracotta sculptures; later masks and textiles.
artsArchitecture.source: Wikipedia: Nok culture; Wikipedia: History of West Africa

socialStructure.source: Wikipedia: Nok culture; Wikipedia: History of West Africa

sharedIdentity.source: Wikipedia: Nok culture; Wikipedia: History of West Africa

dailyLife.value: Round mud houses with thatched roofs in walled family compounds; porridge from millet or sorghum, yams.
dailyLife.source: Wikipedia: Nok culture; Wikipedia: History of West Africa

neighbours.value: Saharan peoples, the forest peoples of the coast, later the Ghana, Mali and Songhai empires.
neighbours.source: Wikipedia: Nok culture; Wikipedia: History of West Africa

ideasReligions.value: Islam spread from about the 11th century through traders.
ideasReligions.source: Wikipedia: Nok culture; Wikipedia: History of West Africa

colonisation.value: Colonised by France and Britain in the late 19th century.
colonisation.source: Wikipedia: Nok culture; Wikipedia: History of West Africa

riseSignals.value: Dhar Tichitt in Mauritania was settled by pastoralists and farmers from about 2000 to 300 BCE; the Nok culture of Nigeria may have lasted from 1500 BCE to 1 BCE. The entry’s start of 2500 BCE is earlier than both.
riseSignals.source: Wikipedia: Dhar Tichitt and Nok culture (checked 13 Nov 2026)

peakPeriod.value: No single peak; kingdoms rose from these farming societies.
peakPeriod.source: Wikipedia: Nok culture; Wikipedia: History of West Africa

declineSignals.value: Not a single society, so no single decline.
declineSignals.source: Wikipedia: Nok culture; Wikipedia: History of West Africa

outcome.value: Around 2,500 years ago the Sahara dried out near Dhar Tichitt and people are thought to have been forced out; the page gives no reason for the Nok decline.

sources.value: Wikipedia: Nok culture; Wikipedia: History of West Africa.
sources.source: Wikipedia: Nok culture; Wikipedia: History of West Africa

overallCertainty.value: Mostly known from archaeology; dates are approximate.
overallCertainty.source: Wikipedia: Nok culture; Wikipedia: History of West Africa
